text:
alex: quick check — I'm getting a 401 on curl against hosted API but the same API_KEY works from our node SDK. header looks like `Authorization: Basic <base64>` when i print it. anyone seen weird invisible chars in env vars?

maria: can you paste the exact curl (sanitized) and how you're constructing the header? sometimes echo adds a newline.

alex: sure — here's what i'm running locally:```bash
export RD_API_KEY=pk_live_ABC123...
curl -H "Authorization: Basic $(echo -n "$RD_API_KEY:" | base64)" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
```
returns 401. if i run node sdk with process.env.RD_API_KEY it works.

sam: curious — you used `echo -n` which should avoid newline. what's the base64 output vs what the SDK sends? try printing raw bytes. could be BOM or non-breaking space.

alex: how do i check for BOM? i tried `cat -v` and it looked normal.

maria: `cat -v` won't show U+FEFF. try `xxd -g 1 -u` or `od -An -t x1` on the env var:```bash
printf '%s' "$RD_API_KEY:" | od -An -t x1
```
if you see `ef bb bf` at the start that's UTF-8 BOM (U+FEFF).

alex: ran it and got: `ef bb bf 70 6b 5f 6c 69 76 65 ...` ohh that's BOM. how did that get in there?

sam: common when copying from some docs or a Windows file. also editors like Notepad can insert BOM. Quick fix: strip it when exporting:```bash
# remove BOM and any weird whitespace
export RD_API_KEY=$(printf '%s' "$RD_API_KEY" | sed 's/^\xef\xbb\xbf//; s/[[:space:]]*$//')
```
then `printf '%s' "$RD_API_KEY:" | base64` should match what SDK sends.

maria: also prefer `printf '%s'` to `echo` — and always include the trailing colon before base64 (token + ":"). examples:```bash
# correct header construction
AUTH="Basic $(printf '%s' "$RD_API_KEY:" | base64)"
# curl
curl -H "Authorization: $AUTH" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

alex: that fixed it, thx! curious — CI picked up the same key from Vault and didn't have BOM. maybe copy/paste into env during local testing added it.

sam: yep. if you want to prevent future mistakes, we have a small helper in dev-extras to normalise keys on load. also GH Actions secrets strip newlines but won't strip BOM. we should add a linter that runs `printf` + `od` on keys during setup.

ci-bot: note: deploy pipeline uses `rd-secret-sync` to push keys; verify it doesn't introduce BOMs when reading from .env files. (automated check: https://go/rd-secret-sync-rules)

alex: filing a quick follow-up PR to add a check in our local quickstart: trim BOM and show `printf` examples in the README. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
__notes: must be a single string for the thread; messages are newline-separated, prefixed by sender name
